body: Third-party skills can expose LLM agents to malicious instructions hidden by encoding. We introduce Ciphered Skill Injection (CSI), which embeds such instructions in skill files for agents to decode and follow. We evaluate Caesar and layered variants across eight models and 139 injection-task pairs, separating instruction recovery from attack success. In the primary setting with shortened skills, the variants achieve attack success rates of up to 47.5% and 40.3%, respectively. Successful decoding does not guarantee attack success, and layering has model-dependent effects. The tested skill scanners rarely flag injected skills. These findings highlight the risk of promoting decoded, untrusted content into actionable instructions.
summaryZh: 本文介绍了加密技能注入（CSI）攻击，展示了恶意指令如何通过编码隐藏在技能文件中并被LLM代理解码执行。研究评估了多种模型在不同加密变体下的脆弱性，攻击成功率最高达47.5%，强调了对代理执行内容进行严格安全审查的必要性。
